feed.title: [BIP draft] Unspendable Internal Keys for Wallet Policies

entry.title: [BIP draft] Unspendable Internal Keys for Wallet Policies
entry.summary:
The email highlights an important aspect of a proposed Bitcoin Improvement Proposal (BIP) concerning the Taproot outputs. It points out that this construction allows for Taproot outputs to be provably script-path-only after the fact to anyone who is provided with the policy. This feature is particularly relevant in a post-quantum scenario where it could be crucial for proving that a key path was never spendable and thus, validating recovery through a script path.
Currently, under existing protocols, any Pay-to-Taproot (P2TR) output can be spent by a Collision Resistant Quantum Computer (CRQC) that solves a specific problem, Q, regardless of how Q was constructed. This is because on the blockchain, tweaked and untweaked keys appear identical. The proposed BIP, however, embeds the policy itself as part of the evidence required for recovery mechanisms. This means that in cases where the authenticity of a transaction needs to be verified, the holder of the policy can recompute the chain code, derive the internal key from a hash (H), and rebuild Q, whereas an attacker without access to the policy cannot replicate this proof.
Furthermore, the security section of the proposal acknowledges that the derivation from H can be verified by anyone, enhancing the security model. The policy knowledge becomes a pivotal element that a rescue rule might require as proof, offering an additional layer of security and utility. The inclusion of a versioned tag within this framework provides flexibility for future rules to specify versions of the policy, potentially aiding in the enforcement and verification processes.
This feature was discussed in a thread focused on exposure-classification, where the topic of holder-provability for P2TR was raised. The discussions suggest that this BIP could work well in conjunction with other measures to enhance the provability and security of P2TR transactions, making a strong case for its adoption beyond mere interoperability reasons. This perspective may warrant further discussion or a mention in the Motivation section of the proposal to emphasize its importance and broader implications.
